The Sherbrooke Fusilier Regiment was a Canadian armoured regiment formed in 1940 from two Sherbrooke militia units and converted to armour in 1942; its lineage continues through the Sherbrooke Hussars. Under Lieutenant-Colonel Mel Gordon, it landed at Juno Beach on 6 June 1944 and fought through Normandy, including the battles around Authie, Buron and Caen, suffering heavy losses while supporting Canadian infantry. Its Sherman tank Bomb survived the war from D-Day to May 1945 and is preserved in Canada as a memorial.

Ellen White is a former English forward and England’s record goalscorer, known for winning the WSL Golden Boot and representing England at three World Cups and Great Britain at two Olympics. Across a club career with Arsenal, Chelsea, Leeds Carnegie, Notts County, Birmingham City and Manchester City, she won major domestic trophies and was named England Women’s Player of the Year three times. Raised in Aylesbury, she began playing football as a child, made her senior England debut in 2010, and retired in 2022 after winning the UEFA Women’s Euro.

Chemical equilibrium occurs when a system’s free energy is minimized, and equilibrium constants relate this condition to species’ activities, concentrations, or gas fugacities; the constants depend on temperature and, for concentration-based definitions, solution conditions such as ionic strength. Known equilibrium constants and mass balances allow the concentrations of all species in a mixture to be calculated, while experimental measurements and nonlinear fitting are used to determine unknown constants. These principles underpin applications including acid–base, host–guest, metal-complex, solubility, and redox chemistry, as well as industrial processes such as ammonia synthesis.

Gabriel & Dresden, the electronic duo of Josh Gabriel and Dave Dresden, formed in 2001 and became known for acclaimed remixes, chart-topping dance hits, and awards, including two IDMA honors for Best American DJ. After releasing their debut album in 2006, they split in 2008, pursued separate projects, and reunited in 2011; later albums included *The Only Road* (2017) and *Remedy* (2020). Their contrasting backgrounds—Dresden’s extensive DJ and music-industry experience and Gabriel’s expertise in composition, synthesizers, and music technology—helped shape their sound and career.

After the Korean War, South Korea and the U.S. military tolerated and regulated prostitution in military camptowns, despite laws banning it; women working there faced severe stigma and were known by a range of often derogatory terms. The system expanded amid postwar poverty and was supported by government policies that treated camptowns as special districts and promoted sex work as a source of foreign currency, while women endured monitoring, health examinations, and racialized discrimination. Estimates of the number of sex workers vary widely, but figures generally show a decline alongside the reduction in U.S. troop numbers, even as camptown prostitution remained economically and politically significant.

The Used released *In Love and Death* on September 28, 2004; the platinum-certified album remains their most commercially successful and was the last to feature drummer Branden Steineckert. Recorded amid band tensions and the deaths of two friends—including vocalist Bert McCracken’s pregnant ex-girlfriend Kate—the album explores loss, love, regret, and personal reflection through an eclectic emo, punk, and alternative rock sound. Promoted with singles such as “Take It Away,” “All That I’ve Got,” and “I Caught Fire,” it was also reissued with the charity cover “Under Pressure,” recorded with My Chemical Romance. B3H-X6LG

George Awsumb was a Norwegian-American architect whose eclectic work ranged from neoclassical and Prairie School designs to Gothic Revival and International Style buildings. After studying architecture and traveling in Europe, he moved to Memphis in 1919, where he designed major public buildings and churches, including the Memphis Municipal Auditorium and Idlewild Presbyterian Church. His sons and grandson continued the family practice, contributing generations of architectural work to Memphis and the surrounding region.

Ellen White is a retired English forward and the England women’s national team’s record goalscorer, known for her prolific club career with Arsenal, Birmingham City and Manchester City. She won multiple domestic trophies, earned the WSL Golden Boot in 2017–18, and represented England at three World Cups, helping the team finish third in 2015 and reach the semi-finals in 2019. A three-time England Women’s Player of the Year, she retired in August 2022 after winning the European Championship with England.

The U.S. military and South Korean authorities tolerated and regulated prostitution around military bases despite its legal prohibition, with women subjected to stigma, health monitoring, and low social status. The system expanded amid postwar poverty and was formally supported through policies and programs that framed the women’s work as economically useful, even patriotic, while estimates of their numbers varied widely over time. From the 1990s, many Korean women were replaced by migrant women, and advocacy around these camptown workers diverged from activism for victims of Japanese military sexual slavery.

Dale Abbey, near Ilkeston in Derbyshire, became a Premonstratensian abbey in 1204 after several earlier attempts to establish a religious community at Deepdale. Its 13th-century chronicle, written by Thomas de Muskham, mixes foundation legends of hermits, visions and an outlaw with a more practical account of local landowners’ efforts to create a religious house. The abbey later acquired extensive regional lands and church revenues, but its discipline declined; despite accusations of misconduct, it paid a fine to remain open until its dissolution in 1538.

Joseph Ganim, a Democrat, served as Bridgeport’s mayor from 1991 until resigning in 2003 after a federal conviction for corruption, then returned to office after winning the 2015 election. During his first tenure, he pursued crime reduction and urban redevelopment, but was convicted of accepting more than $500,000 in kickbacks from contractors and served seven years in prison. He later won reelection in 2019 and 2024 and is currently serving his seventh term; he also unsuccessfully sought Connecticut’s Democratic gubernatorial nomination in 1994 and 2018.

Our World was the first live multinational, multi-satellite television broadcast, airing in 24 countries on 25 June 1967 to an estimated 400–700 million viewers. Coordinated by the BBC and the European Broadcasting Union, it involved 14 national broadcasters, four satellites, and thousands of people, with every segment required to be live and free of political figures. Its international program featured cultural and everyday-life segments from around the world, most famously the Beatles’ first performance of “All You Need Is Love.”

El Salvador’s electricity system relies heavily on thermal, hydroelectric and geothermal generation, with geothermal production the highest in Central America; rising demand and exposure to oil prices have driven plans to expand renewable capacity and diversify supply. The government has promoted hydro, geothermal, solar, wind and biomass projects, alongside regional integration through SIEPAC, while working to extend rural electrification and improve access. The document also describes a major 2025 shift toward tighter government control of the electricity market, including oversight of contracts and pricing, against a backdrop of historically divided public and private sector roles.

There is no universal extremum principle that predicts far-from-equilibrium steady states; proposed principles generally depend on a system’s specific constraints and often apply only locally or under restricted conditions. Inexact macroscopic descriptions leave many microscopic states unspecified, producing apparent fluctuations that can drive dynamical structures; entropy is presented chiefly as a measure of how reproducible experimental outcomes are, rather than of “order.” The document also surveys limits of classical non-equilibrium thermodynamics, including nonlinear and discontinuous flows, and historical examples of dissipation principles and coupled thermal, electrical, and diffusion effects.

Its segments showcased people, places, science and the arts worldwide, most famously the Beatles’ first performance of “All You Need Is Love.”

Wilson McCoy (1902–1961) was an American illustrator and painter who built a successful commercial art career before becoming the second artist to draw *The Phantom*, taking over from Ray Moore during World War II. He worked on the strip from 1941 until illness ended his work in 1961, with his wife Dorothy assisting on lettering and borders; his Barrington home later served as a model for Diana Palmer’s house. An adventurous traveler who researched stories abroad, McCoy drew inspiration from his journeys, including visits to Central Africa that informed the Phantom’s Bandar tribe.

Yatterman is a 1977–1979 Japanese anime and the longest series in Tatsunoko Productions’ Time Bokan franchise, following young mechanics Gan and Ai as masked heroes who try to stop the Doronbo gang from collecting the Skull Stone. Its episodic adventures parody real-world people and places rather than involving time travel, and feature a range of themed robots, including the dog-shaped Yatterwan. The franchise later received a 2008 television remake, a 2009 live-action film, and the 2015 series Yatterman Night.

Charles Baudelaire’s *Les Fleurs du mal*, first published in 1857, is a landmark of French poetry whose innovative forms and themes of decadence, suffering, death, and idealism influenced Symbolism, Modernism, and later poets. Its frank content led to a prosecution, a fine, and the suppression of six poems; the 1861 edition added *Tableaux Parisiens*, which portrays the alienation of people in a rapidly modernizing Paris. The collection has inspired numerous translations and adaptations in music, film, and other art forms.

Roza Shanina was a Soviet sniper in World War II who volunteered after her brother’s death, trained with distinction, and joined the front in 1944 despite efforts to keep snipers out of heavy fighting. Renowned for her accuracy and rapid double shots, she was credited with more than 50 kills and became the first woman on the 3rd Belorussian Front to receive the Order of Glory. She was killed in January 1945 while protecting a severely wounded artillery commander, and her wartime diary was published after the war.

NORSOC, Norway’s special operations unit, was established in 1982 to address terrorism risks and evolved from earlier military ranger and parachute units; in 2014, it was placed alongside the Naval Special Operations Commando under a joint special operations command. Its duties include counterterrorism and support to police, and it has served in Kosovo and Afghanistan, including hostage rescue and training Afghan forces. The unit recruits through demanding physical and mental selection followed by a year of basic training, and has used specialized vehicles including Geländewagen platforms and Supacat HMT Extendas.

Sectoral balances are an accounting framework showing that government, private-sector, and foreign-sector financial balances must sum to zero. A government deficit adds net financial assets to the non-government sector, while a surplus removes them; the foreign balance reflects the counterpart of the current account. The framework is used to interpret economic shifts and policy, including how private saving, trade imbalances, and government budgets interact, and why austerity during downturns may be counterproductive.

The Tour de Ski is an annual multi-stage FIS cross-country skiing competition held in Central Europe, featuring varied race formats and concluding with a climb up Alpe Cermis in Val di Fiemme. Overall standings are determined by cumulative times, adjusted for bonus seconds, alongside separate points and climbing classifications. First held in 2006–07, the event has grown into a major season highlight, with Tobias Angerer and Virpi Kuitunen its first overall winners and several later champions dominating multiple editions.

Mexico’s nationality laws evolved substantially from independence through the 20th century, with rules often tying women’s nationality to their husbands and later reforms gradually ending that practice. The document also notes restrictions on certain public offices for dual nationals and reports that, in 2018, Mexican passport holders had visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 159 destinations.

The framework applies across acid–base, host–guest, metal-complex, solubility, gas-phase, and redox systems, with practical uses ranging from chemical sensing and drug discovery to industrial synthesis and chelation therapy.

“Birthday Cake” is a sexually explicit R&B interlude on Rihanna’s 2011 album *Talk That Talk*, included after fans pushed for its release despite its brief 1:18 length. A full-length remix featuring Chris Brown premiered on Rihanna’s 24th birthday in 2012, drew controversy because of their relationship history, and helped the song reach number 24 on the Billboard Hot 100. Critics were divided over its lyrics and short format; the track was certified double platinum in the US and later performed on tour and on *Saturday Night Live*.

Şanlıurfa is a largely Kurdish, semi-arid province in southeastern Turkey, where the state-sponsored GAP project expanded irrigation through a system of dams and river diversions. Agriculture dominates the economy, especially cotton, pistachios, grains, and peppers, while irrigation has boosted production but also contributed to soil salinity; food processing, textiles, trade, and transport are other important sectors. The province has high population growth, large households, low literacy—particularly among women—and substantial out-migration, while also hosting Turkey’s largest Syrian refugee population, many of whom work in agriculture, construction, and commerce; local cultural and linguistic similarities have helped ease tensions. His youthful image of chasing a beam of light helped him sense a conflict between Newtonian mechanics and Maxwell’s constant speed of light, though its historical interpretation is debated. The magnet-and-conductor induction example later highlighted his conviction that equivalent observations should not depend on which object is moving, helping motivate special relativity.

Founded as an industrial hub in the 1950s, it developed around major public-sector enterprises and remains an important economic centre, though several factories have closed or struggled. In 2011, its municipal corporation had about 581,000 residents, with high literacy and a predominantly Bengali-speaking, Hindu population.

Their authenticity was disputed from the outset, and later scholars concluded that he had substantially adapted or invented the material, though the controversy helped popularise Gaelic culture. He also wrote historical and political works, served in Parliament and as a government pamphleteer, and later acquired Highland estates that were criticised for contributing to the clearances.

His administration included prominent figures such as Baltasar Brum, and Viera received France’s Legion of Honor in 1916.

Tomohito Oda’s manga *Komi Can’t Communicate* follows Shoko Komi, a high school student with severe social anxiety, and classmate Hitohito Tadano as they work toward her goal of making 100 friends. Critics and audiences have praised its humor and compassionate portrayal of social anxiety, though some have criticized certain character-based jokes; the anime also won Best Comedy at the Crunchyroll Anime Awards.

“Birthday Cake” is an R&B interlude on Rihanna’s 2011 album *Talk That Talk*, expanded into a full-length remix featuring Chris Brown and released as a US single in 2012. Its sexually explicit lyrics and brief original version drew mixed reviews, with critics both praising its provocative style and criticizing its content and abrupt ending. The song reached number 24 on the Billboard Hot 100, was certified double platinum in the US, and was performed on Rihanna’s tours and *Saturday Night Live*.

Feliciano Viera was a Colorado Party politician and close ally of José Batlle y Ordóñez, rising from local and parliamentary offices to become interior minister and president of the Senate. Nominated by the Batllista majority, he served as Uruguay’s president from 1915 to 1919, leading a government that supported the Allied cause in World War I and strengthened ties with the United States. His career also included legislative work on rural taxation and advocacy for constitutional reform, though Batlle and some contemporaries questioned his political judgment and associations.

Yatterman is a 108-episode Japanese anime that aired from 1977 to 1979 as part of Tatsunoko Productions’ Time Bokan franchise, later inspiring a 2008 remake, a 2009 live-action film, and the 2015 series Yatterman Night. The story follows young mechanics Gan and Ai, who become the heroes Yatterman-1 and Yatterman-2 and use their robot allies to stop the Doronbo gang from collecting fragments of the Skull Stone in pursuit of hidden gold. Known for its themed mecha battles, comedic villains, and parodies of real-world people and places, the series features a wide range of animal-shaped robots and recurring characters.

Inter, one of Ukraine’s most widely watched TV channels, was founded in 1996 and is now part of Inter Media Group, owned by oligarch Dmytro Firtash; its international service, Inter Plus, has served Ukrainians abroad. After Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, Inter joined the state-coordinated United News telethon, while financial difficulties later led to plans to close several European bureaus and cut staff. The channel has faced recurring criticism and protests over alleged censorship, political influence, and Russian programming, alongside changes in ownership and management.

Dale Abbey near Ilkeston began as a hermitage, according to a detailed but partly legendary 13th-century chronicle, and was formally founded in 1204 as a Premonstratensian house. It grew into an influential regional abbey, acquiring estates and parish churches, though its discipline and reputation fluctuated, and it survived the 1536 dissolution threshold by paying a fine before closing in 1538. The chronicle credits local hermits and landowners with its early development, describing successive attempts to establish a religious community at Deepdale before its eventual incorporation into the Augustinian community at Calke Priory.

Sectoral balances are an accounting framework showing that the government, domestic private, and foreign sectors’ financial balances must sum to zero: a deficit in one sector is matched by surpluses elsewhere. In 2019, the U.S. had a private-sector surplus of 4.4% of GDP and a foreign-sector surplus of 2.8% (from its current-account deficit), matched by a government deficit of 7.2%. The framework helps explain how shifts in private saving and investment can drive government deficits, and why austerity during downturns may worsen conditions, though the accounting identity alone does not establish causation.
